chunks: Only the wretch will turn aside from it,

key_terms.الْأَشْقَىٰ: The wretched one, one destined for misery in the Hereafter
key_terms.يَتَجَنَّبُهَا: He turns aside from it, avoids it

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'wretch' that turns aside from the Book in Surah Al-A'la?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *al-ashqa* (the wretched one) as the antithesis of *al-sa'ad* (the happy one), emphasizing the pre-eternal decree (*al-jabr wa al-tafwid*) regarding spiritual destiny. The term 'turns aside' (*yatajannabu*) implies a deliberate, active avoidance of the Quranic message, reflecting the inner state of those whose hearts are sealed due to persistent rejection. This highlights the dualistic outcome of human choice within divine foreknowledge, a key theme in Usuli and Akhbari discussions on predestination.
